matrix_character.definition: Lean animal tissue dominated by protein
matrix_character.prep_implication: Alkaline or enzymatic digestion usually sufficient
Lipid residue can blind filters and spectra; may need lipid removal step

matrix_character.definition: Heterogeneous organic and mineral material from the digestive tract
matrix_character.prep_implication: May need density separation for mineral particles
Heme and protein removal; small volumes limit detection

matrix_character.definition: Low-solids fluids such as urine or lavage
matrix_character.prep_implication: Often filtered directly after mild digestion

matrix_character.definition: Mixed organic; fibre and mineral content
matrix_character.prep_implication: Strong oxidative digestion plus density separation are common
Acid dissolution of carbonate may damage some polymers
Cellulose resists alkaline digestion; oxidative or enzymatic steps

matrix_character.definition: Whole bodies including exoskeleton or chitin
matrix_character.prep_implication: Chitin and shell fragments may persist after digestion
Depends on product; dissolution or digestion
No digestion; limited to imaging-based identification

finding_role.definition: Polymer reported in a biological (or food) sample that was not deliberately exposed
Known polymer deliberately given to organisms or cells and then measured
Known polymer added to test recovery of the method
Polymer used to develop or demonstrate the method outside the biological samples
Material used for comparison (e.g. natural fibre)
Material added to test false positives
Polymer found in procedural or field blanks and not in samples
Named in the reference library without evidence of detection
Polymer targeted by the method and not detected (below detection limit)
Polymer targeted but not reported for a stated reason (e.g. blank contamination)
Polymer removed from the analytical panel
Polymer identified in water / sediment / debris samples of the same study
Particle identified as a natural or non-plastic material
Polymer named only as a possible source in the discussion
Extraction text names the polymer with a caution word; not yet checked against the paper
Default for extraction-based rows whose role has not been checked

evidence_status.definition: Identity and presence supported by the full text
Authors describe the identification as probable or indicative
Reported but cannot be separated from contamination
Above detection limit but not quantifiable
The paper is inconsistent or unspecific about the material identity
Identity known because the material was added by the investigators
Known material followed by a label or proxy (metal / dye / isotope)
Status does not apply to this role

polymer_outcome.definition: At least one polymer identified in study samples
Polymers assigned but their origin in the sample is uncertain
Identification attempted and no polymer confirmed (within the stated size scope)
Identification was done on other material (e.g. debris) not on the biological sample
No polymer identity reported and no explicit statement about identification

qaqc_item.definition: Method or procedural blanks processed alongside samples
Open filters or dishes monitoring airborne contamination in the lab
Instrument, pyrolysis, solvent or reagent blanks
How sample results were corrected for blanks
Whether the contribution of blanks to final results was assessed
Lab coats or clothing that do not shed synthetic fibres
Clean room / laminar-flow hood / standard lab
Study reports a spike recovery or extraction efficiency
Recovery tested in the same kind of matrix as the samples
Final results adjusted by the measured recovery
A limit of detection is defined or reported
A limit of quantification is defined or reported
Certified or other reference material analysed
A second independent technique confirmed or complemented the results
Misclassification or false-positive risk is discussed
Raw spectra shared in a reusable format or as images only

analyte_group.definition: Total particles counted regardless of polymer
Sum of polymer masses reported by the study
Anthropogenic or microlitter particles not confirmed as a specific polymer

refmat_type.definition: Plastic issued with an official certificate for a polymer property (mass fraction, size or number) by a reference body (e.g. BAM, JRC, NIST)
Purchased plastic beads, powders, fibres or films with supplier specifications but no reference-material certificate
Polymer standards and kits (e.g. polymer-in-CaCO3) and isotope-labelled internal standards used to calibrate mass spectrometry
Particles or spiked matrices prepared by the study team (cryo-milled, weathered, synthesised, spiked blood or synthetic faeces)
Instrument standards (silicon, gold nanoparticles, thermal standards) and certified materials for metals or isotopes

refmat_use.definition: Calibration curves or quantification of polymer mass or number
Positive controls and checks of instrument or method performance
Reference for spectral or pyrolysis-product identification
Particles of known size for sizing or size limits
Wavenumber, transport-efficiency, temperature or other instrument calibration
Used for metals, isotopes or other non-plastic analytes

ortho_relation.definition: Each method supplied different information (e.g. mass vs particle count, size, shape)
A second method confirmed or verified the polymer identity or presence
Methods applied to different particle size fractions
Only a subset of counted particles was chemically identified
The methods disagreed or one overestimated (e.g. false positives)
Identification relied on a single analytical platform
Several methods were used but their results were not compared directly
